extracted.intended_audience: researchers (especially computational biologists), authors of published papers, and readers interested in post-publication peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Practices and norms for conducting public, technically grounded critiques of published scientific papers (illustrated by a computational biology researcher's blog). Emphasizes transparency, attribution, and methodological/statistical defensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public, named, technical critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Public, named, technical critiques of high-profile published papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques should be posted publicly and attributed (named author), and focus on technical/statistical/methodological issues in the paper. The blog serves as a working example of this practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical and methodological transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Demands statistical and methodological transparency (e.g., the 'P-value Prize' for justifying claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers should provide data, code, and clear methodological justification so statistical claims can be evaluated. The blog rewards/spotlights cases where statistical claims are or are not properly justified (example: 'P-value Prize').

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication review as continuation of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Treats post-publication review as a legitimate continuation of the peer-review process — not as harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-publication critique is framed as scholarly follow-up to pre-publication review and should be conducted respectfully and professionally; it should aim at correction and instruction rather than personal attack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenter contact requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Valid email required (commenter can be otherwise anonymized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must include a valid email address for accountability; the blog allows commenters to remain publicly anonymized while retaining contactability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation / reject inappropriate content
rubrics_metrics.description: Reserves the right to reject inappropriate content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site maintainers may remove or refuse comments/posts that are off-topic, abusive, or otherwise inappropriate; moderation is part of maintaining constructive post-publication review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing responsibility of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: A reviewer's job doesn't end at acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers and reviewers are encouraged to continue evaluating work after publication, pointing out errors, limitations, or necessary clarifications as part of scientific self-correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution conditional on methodological grounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Public critique with attribution is acceptable when methodologically grounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attributing critiques to named reviewers is appropriate provided the critique is supported by methodological or statistical analysis; anonymous or unsubstantiated attacks are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensibility of statistical claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical claims must be defensible on demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any claim that relies on statistical evidence should be backed by reproducible analyses, data availability, and clear explanation so that others can verify or refute the claim.
